app.title: NanoCore Editor
app.subtitle: Unofficial online editor for the Livtra NanoCore mini multi-effect processor
app.noHardwareNotice: No NanoCore connected yet — build your patch and try it in the Simulator. Switch to Web MIDI once your hardware arrives.

connection.title: MIDI Connection
connection.noOutputs: No MIDI outputs found. Connect your NanoCore via USB and refresh.
connection.channelHint: Must match the NanoCore's own MIDI Channel setting (device channel 0 = Omni, any channel works).

routing.warning: FX2 is set to {{type}}, which reuses MOD's parameter CCs (68-73). Editing MOD parameters right now will actually change FX2's {{type}} instead.

preset.title: Preset Library
preset.sendToDeviceHint: Transmits every block's on/off, type and parameter CC for the current patch. Remember to save it on the device afterwards (long-press MASTER) if you want it to persist.
preset.empty: No saved presets yet. Build a patch and click "Save as new preset".
preset.recallHint: Program Change only tells the NanoCore which of its own stored presets to load — it does not read the resulting parameters back into this editor.

tuner.title: Tuner
tuner.note: Sends CC80 (0 = off, 127 = on) to remotely open/close the on-device tuner. The reference pitch (default 440Hz) is only adjustable on the device itself — no CC is documented for it.

global.title: Global Settings (device reference)
global.hint: These are set on the device itself or via the official companion app — no MIDI CC is documented for them. Mirror your hardware's values here just to keep track.

log.title: MIDI Activity
log.empty: Nothing sent yet. Move a control to see outgoing MIDI messages here.

info.title: About the NanoCore
info.hint: Reference material from Livtra's own documentation — nothing on this page is editable or transmitted, it's here so you don't have to dig through the PDF.
info.bluetoothIntro: The NanoCore has a fully independent dual-mode Bluetooth module. Both modes can be turned on or off independently without interfering with each other.
info.bluetoothNote: The NanoCore MIDI module stays hidden until first paired from within the official mobile app; it only appears in your phone's Bluetooth settings after that initial pairing succeeds.
info.usbAudioText: The device is a driver-free class-compliant USB audio interface — connect it to a computer and it shows up automatically as "Nanocore". It also supports direct connection to phones/tablets via USB OTG for high-quality on-the-go recording and live streaming.
info.companionSoftwareText: Livtra also publishes a free official companion app for comprehensive device management: tone adjustment, preset import/export, NAM (Neural Amp Modeler) file import, third-party IR loading, and factory reset.

bluetoothMode.NanoCore Audio (BT Audio): Receives media audio from a phone or tablet. Once connected, your phone's music can be used as a backing track routed into the effects processor.
bluetoothMode.NanoCore MIDI (Wireless MIDI): Connects to the official mobile app for bidirectional parameter sync, control and editing — the wireless counterpart to this editor.
